per_window.ps-ns: unresolved: 15N R1 at 10 °C varies mainly in the 65-73 loop, but model-free fitting failed and no S2 exists (CYPA-J15, r34). MD places Phe113 rotamer exchange at nanoseconds to microseconds and is filed under undetermined (CYPA-J16, r29, md_only).
per_window.us-ms: dynamic_in_window: free WT at 10 °C has an active-site/core group (kex 1,140 s-1) and a 65-84 loop group (kex 2,260 s-1), pB about 5-7% or less (r1, r2); deuterated 600/900 MHz data show 75, 48 and 40 exchanging amides at 0, 10 and 20 °C with per-residue rates of about 1,000-6,000 s-1 at 20 °C (CYPA-J21, CYPA-J4, CYPA-J22; r10-r12, r33, s1); CPMG/R1rho gives 2,200 s-1, pB 2.0% (r38). Exchange persists with CsA, substrate and TA-peptide (r3, r4, r35-r37) and in S99T, rescue and D66A mutants (r9, r22-r24, r39). T-jump SAXS adds microsecond global relaxations (r26). The 2002 R2 survey at 25 °C missed the active-site residues (r5, r6), a sensitivity difference. Phosphate buffer is an untested condition (see buffer_note).
per_window.slower_than_ms: not_measured for the free WT enzyme (CYPA-J19); seconds-scale rates in the rows (kiso 10.4 s-1, capsid 10 s-1) are substrate cis/trans kinetics.
per_window.undetermined: MD (r29) places Phe113 rotamer exchange on the ns-us scale (CYPA-J16, md_only). dynamic_in_window (structure_only): ambient and XFEL crystals show alternates for R55, M61, L98, S99, F113 (r7, r16-r21, s5, s7); cooling to 180 K or below removes most of them (r8, r13-r15, s6).

protein_summary.buffer_note: Untested condition, not a suspected artefact: every apo NMR data set in the rows was recorded in 50 mM sodium phosphate pH 6.5 (Eisenmesser 2002, r5; Eisenmesser 2005, r1-r4; Schlegel 2009, r10-r12; Holliday 2015, r33-r37, with 1 mM EDTA), and none of these sources reports a phosphate-free buffer control, so an anion-binding contribution to the observed exchange is neither shown nor excluded. Crystal data used HEPES/PEG (r7, r13-r21).
protein_summary.wt_apo_answer: Yes: at 10 °C free wild-type CypA exchanges on the microsecond-millisecond scale in an active-site/core network (R55, S99, E120 amides; L39, I57, L98, A103 methyls) at kex 1,140 ± 200 s-1 and in the 65-84 loop at kex 2,260 ± 200 s-1, with a minor state of at most about 7% (5% from methyl fits); deuterated 900 MHz data extend exchange to about half the residues, with per-residue kex of about 1,000-6,000 s-1 measured at 20 °C (r12), not 10 °C, and all of it was recorded in 50 mM sodium phosphate without a buffer control.
open_conflicts: Apo exchange model: two collective processes (group I/II global fits, Eisenmesser 2005, r1) versus a single global two-state process (kex 2,200 ± 90 s-1, pB 2.0 ± 0.1%, combined CPMG/R1rho, r38) versus a segmental continuum of per-residue rates (Schlegel 2009, Holliday 2017, r10-r12, s1); all three are apo WT at 10 °C, all agree exchange exists, and they disagree on how many processes.

Turnover rate meaning: Eisenmesser 2005 equates the 2,730 s-1 turnover kex with on-enzyme isomerization (r3); Holliday 2015 shows binding/release alone gives CPMG exchange (TA-peptide about 300 s-1, r36) and challenges that inference for weak-binding tetrapeptides.

Phe113 network timescale: NMR and crystallography tie Ser99/Phe113 to the millisecond group-I process (r9, r7), while MD finds the Phe113 rotamers interconverting in nanoseconds (r29); different windows, so not a formal conflict, but the assignment is unresolved.
questions_for_gina: Which sample and conditions produced the RelaxDB CYPA_CPMG R2eff labels (source lead EZE/MWC): protonated 15N at 600 MHz and 10 °C (Eisenmesser 2005) or deuterated 600/900 MHz at 0/10/20 °C (Schlegel 2009, Holliday 2015/2017)? The number of exchanging residues differs (fewer than 30 versus 48 at 10 °C).

All apo NMR data (2002, 2005, 2009, 2015) were recorded in 50 mM sodium phosphate pH 6.5 with no phosphate-free control; do you know of a buffer comparison for CypA, or should the exchange be flagged as untested for phosphate binding? (Separately: is 'Gly110' in the 2005 Fig. 1 caption Ser110 or Gly109?)
